description: This is a false-colour infrared satellite image showing a landscape dominated by agricultural fields and natural vegetation. The image features bright red rectangular areas, characteristic of active agricultural plots, indicating vigorous vegetation. Areas of natural vegetation appear in brownish-red and green tones, suggesting scrubland or forests. A dark, curvilinear feature resembling a river or stream is visible in the bottom right, flowing alongside some agricultural land. Two black-outlined polygons highlight specific land cover types. The larger, upper polygon is labelled "Sclerophyllous vegetation" and encompasses an area of brownish-red natural vegetation. A smaller, lower polygon, labelled "sclerophyllous area", outlines another patch of similar vegetation adjacent to the potential river feature. The image depicts a scene potentially in Central Spain, consistent with descriptions of sclerophyllous vegetation, also referred to as *Stipa tenacissima* or *garrigue* and *maquis* in the surrounding context. The imagery credit is Eurostat, from the 2012 Land Use/Cover Area frame Statistical Survey (LUCAS).
